results.project_title: Effectivenss of an Integrated Treatment to Address Smoking Cessation and Anxiety/Depression in People Living with HIV
results.phr_text:
PUBLIC HEALTH NARRATIVE
Smokers living with HIV represent a major health disparity population in the United States (US) and their
unique healthcare needs are not being met. Building from our successful R34 project (1R34DA031038-01A1),
the proposed study aims to address smoking-based health disparity among smokers living with HIV by testing
whether our 9-session, cognitive-behavioral-based intervention (Project QUIT), which addresses smoking by
reducing anxiety/depression via specific emotional vulnerabilities (anxiety sensitivity, distress tolerance, and
anhedonia), outperforms an active, credible time-matched control and a standard-of-care (SOC) control. If
successful, the intervention would be ready for translation studies to examine effectiveness and dissemination
into “real-world” behavioral health, mental health, and social service settings.
